10 月份，在以习近平同志为核心的党中央坚强领导下，各地区各部门认真贯彻落实党中央和国务院决策部署，坚持稳中求进工作总基调，强化存量政策和增量政策协同，扎实推进高质量发展，生产供给平稳增长，市场销售规模扩大，对外贸易快速增长，就业物价总体稳定，新质生产力茁壮成长，国民经济运行延续总体平稳、向新向优发展态势。
10 月份，全国规模以上工业增加值同比增长 4.8% ，环比增长 0.21% 。分三大门类看，采矿业增加值同比增长 0.7% ，制造业增长 5.4% ，电力、热力、燃气及水生产和供应业增长 4.4% 。装备制造业增加值同比增长 10.6% ，高技术制造业增加值增长 17.6% ，分别快于全部规模以上工业增加值 5.8 和 12.8 个百分点。分经济类型看，国有控股企业增加值同比增长 2.1% ；股份制企业增长 5.2% ，外商及港澳台投资企业增长 3.0% ；私营企业增长 3.2% 。分产品看， 3D 打印设备、锂离子电池、工业机器人产品产量同比分别增长 85.9% 、 30.0% 、 26.0% 。 1 — 10 月份，全国规模以上工业增加值同比增长 5.3% 。 10 月份，制造业采购经理指数为 49.3% ，企业生产经营活动预期指数为 53.4% 。 1 — 9 月份，全国规模以上工业企业实现利润总额 60337 亿元，同比增长 15.5% 。
10 月份，全国服务业生产指数同比增长 4.6% 。分行业看，租赁和商务服务业，信息传输、软件和信息技术服务业，交通运输、仓储和邮政业生产指数同比分别增长 9.3% 、 9.2% 、 5.1% 。 1 — 10 月份，全国服务业生产指数同比增长 4.7% 。 10 月份，服务业商务活动指数为 50.0% ，服务业业务活动预期指数为 55.2% 。其中，铁路运输、水上运输、邮政、互联网软件及信息技术服务等行业商务活动指数位于 55.0% 以上较高景气区间。 1 — 9 月份，规模以上服务业企业营业收入同比增长 5.4% 。
1 — 10 月份，社会消费商品和服务零售总额同比增长 2.5% ，其中服务零售额增长 4.9% ，商品零售额增长 0.9% 。在服务零售额中，通讯信息服务类、旅游咨询租赁服务类、文体休闲服务类零售额较快增长。 1 — 10 月份，社会消费品零售总额 416464 亿元，同比增长 1.0% 。 1 — 10 月份，全国网上商品和服务零售额 169811 亿元，同比增长 3.7% 。其中，网上商品零售额 107274 亿元，增长 2.9% ；网上服务零售额 62537 亿元，增长 5.0% 。 10 月份，社会消费品零售总额 46463 亿元，同比增长 0.4% ；环比增长 0.02% 。按经营单位所在地分，城镇消费品零售额 40098 亿元，同比增长 0.2% ；乡村消费品零售额 6365 亿元，增长 1.5% 。按消费类型分，商品零售额 41228 亿元，同比增长 0.3% ；餐饮收入 5235 亿元，增长 0.7% 。部分升级类商品销售较快增长，限额以上单位通讯器材类、文化办公用品类商品零售额同比分别增长 6.5% 、 4.1% 。
1 — 10 月份，全国固定资产投资（不含农户） 364824 亿元，同比下降 8.1% ；扣除房地产开发的固定资产投资下降 5.1% 。其中，知识产权产品投资同比增长 9.2% 。高技术产业投资同比增长 4.0% ，其中信息服务业，航空、航天器及设备制造业，电子及通信设备制造业投资分别增长 20.5% 、 10.2% 、 6.6% 。分产业看，第一产业投资同比下降 6.1% ，第二产业投资下降 3.6% ，第三产业投资下降 10.9% 。分领域看，基础设施投资同比下降 5.1% ，制造业投资下降 2.9% ，房地产开发投资下降 21.6% 。民间投资同比下降 11.4% ；扣除房地产开发的民间投资下降 7.8% 。全国新建商品房销售面积 61358 万平方米，同比下降 13.7% ；新建商品房销售额 58550 亿元，下降 14.3% 。全国二手房交易网签面积 67971 万平方米，同比增长 11.4% 。 10 月份，固定资产投资（不含农户）环比下降 2.93% 。

固定资产投资（不含农户）：是以货币形式表现的在一定时期内完成的建造和购置固定资产的工作量以及与此有关的费用的总称。

在企业的全部实收资本中，国有经济成分的出资人拥有的实收资本（股本）所占比例虽未大于 50% ，但相对大于其他任何一方经济成分的出资人所占比例的国有相对控股；或者虽不大于其他经济成分，但根据协议规定拥有企业实际控制权的国有协议控股。
投资双方各占 50% ，且未明确由谁绝对控股的企业，若其中一方为国有经济成分的，一律按国有控股处理。
登记注册统计类别：按照国家统计局、国家市场监督管理总局联合印发《关于市场主体统计分类的划分规定》（国统字〔 2023 〕 14 号）执行。

Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have

items.excerpt:
I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone , which is now 53% complete.
The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method.
There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory : private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed).
There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0 . A new Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai , Peter Olkhovets , Ilya Khalafi , and Ankita Advitot .

DHL Supply Chain is testing adaptive AI-powered robots and introducing AI orchestration into live warehouse operations as part of a wider strategy to coordinate robotics, artificial intelligence and human workers across its global logistics network.
The initiatives form part of the company’s Intelligent Supply Chain framework, which aims to move beyond automating individual tasks toward coordinating entire warehouse workflows.
Unlike conventional warehouse robots that largely follow predefined instructions, adaptive robots are designed to interpret changing conditions and adjust their actions to achieve specific goals.
DHL says it is testing these capabilities alongside AI orchestration software that connects employees, automated equipment and operational data.
Following a successful proof of concept, the company has begun introducing the orchestration technology into operational warehouses.
One application being tested combines autonomous mobile robots, packaging equipment and warehouse management systems to allocate resources dynamically according to changing order volumes.
The system is intended to help warehouse operators respond to demand fluctuations while improving throughput and operational flexibility.
Tim Tetzlaff, global head of digital transformation at DHL Supply Chain, says: “Our immediate priority is to continue scaling our proven robotics across more sites while moving the next generation of adaptive AI-powered robotics from pilots into live operations.”
DHL has already installed more than 9,000 robots across its global logistics network, completing more than 1.5 billion robotic picks.
Its operations have also recorded 10 million robotic case unloads using Boston Dynamics’ Stretch robot.
The company says more than 95 percent of its warehouses worldwide now use advanced digitalization technologies.

items.excerpt:
Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, an updated vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots’ ability to perform complex physical tasks in industrial and everyday environments.
The company says the new model expands the range of tasks robots can perform while improving dexterity, reliability and safety.
Gemini Robotics 2.5 was evaluated across more than 200 tasks, including handling delicate objects, using tools, manipulating flexible materials and performing precision assembly operations.
According to Google DeepMind, the model achieved success rates 30 to 100 percent higher than previous versions, depending on the task, while completing operations 20 to 30 percent faster.
One of the most significant demonstrations involved Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot operating on Mercedes-Benz production lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany.
The robots performed automotive kitting, which involves selecting individual components from bulk containers and arranging them into trays for vehicle assembly.
Using Gemini Robotics 2.5 to control its arms and hands, alongside Gemini Robotics ER for task planning, Apollo 2 achieved a reported 96 percent success rate during the proof-of-concept program.
Jeff Cardenas, co-founder and CEO of Apptronik, says: “This is what we built Apollo for: useful work alongside people in real industrial settings.
“Pairing Apollo 2 with Gemini Robotics, we saw the models improve dramatically in just a few weeks of post-training and carry over to Mercedes-Benz production with very little drop-off. This is the foundation for bringing humanoid robots to industrial and commercial environments at scale.”
Google DeepMind has also introduced improvements intended to help robots operate safely around obstacles and people.
The company reports that new reasoning-based safety controls increased safe task completion by 33 percent around obstacles and 43 percent when people were nearby.
Separately, it introduced ASIMOV-Jailbreak, an open-source benchmark designed to evaluate whether robotics AI systems resist instructions that could lead to unsafe actions.
Google DeepMind says its Gemini 4 Argon model achieved 99.5 percent resistance in these evaluations, compared with 82 percent for its previous baseline.

items.excerpt:
Avride says its autonomous delivery robots have completed one million deliveries across the United States, marking a milestone in the company’s expansion into urban neighborhoods and university campuses.
The company reported completing 180,000 deliveries in October alone, while its operations have reached a daily volume of 7,000 deliveries.
Avride currently operates in more than 30 markets across the US, including Austin, Dallas, Jersey City, Philadelphia and Miami.
Its delivery robots are integrated with established food delivery platforms, including Uber Eats and Grubhub, allowing customers to order food through existing applications.
In a company blog post announcing the milestone, Avride said: “This milestone shows Avride’s momentum as it expands across city neighborhoods and university campuses.”
The company also highlighted the operational challenges involved in providing autonomous delivery services across different environments, from university campuses to busy urban sidewalks.
As Avride explained: “Each setting brings different demands. A campus lunch rush, a busy neighborhood sidewalk, and a restaurant’s evening pickup all require technology and operations that work together.”
The delivery process involves restaurant staff loading orders into robots, which then navigate to their destinations. Customers can track deliveries and unlock the robots’ cargo compartments through the participating delivery applications.
Avride attributes its growth to coordination between its engineering, manufacturing and operations teams, alongside its commercial delivery partners.
The company says it plans to continue expanding its autonomous delivery network while improving services for restaurants, university dining operations and customers.
The milestone comes as sidewalk delivery robots become an increasingly established part of last-mile logistics, particularly for short-distance food deliveries in urban areas.

items.excerpt:
Wing has launched its drone delivery service in the Memphis metropolitan area in partnership with Walmart , extending its autonomous delivery network into Tennessee for the first time.
The service is available to tens of thousands of households across parts of Tennessee and Arkansas, allowing eligible customers to order groceries, household products and other everyday essentials for delivery by drone.
Customers can choose from thousands of Walmart products, with orders arriving in as little as 30 minutes, according to the companies.
The initial rollout covers neighborhoods surrounding three Walmart Supercenters in Bartlett and Cordova, Tennessee, and West Memphis, Arkansas.
Heather Rivera, chief business officer at Wing, says: “We’re proud to have the opportunity to show up as a helpful, good neighbor for residents throughout the Memphis metro. Starting today, local families have a faster, more convenient option for last-minute groceries and daily necessities, while helping ease neighborhood traffic.”

Paris-based startup Physicl has raised $10 million in seed funding to develop technology that helps robotics and physical AI researchers identify and address weaknesses in their AI models.
The funding round was led by Inovia Capital, with participation from US Venture Partners, and will support the expansion of Physicl’s team and further development of its synthetic data generation platform.
The company has also introduced Studio, an application that allows researchers to create customized 3D environments and generate training data targeting specific situations in which AI models struggle.
One of the challenges facing physical AI developers is preparing models to operate reliably in unpredictable real-world environments.
Although models can perform well in controlled demonstrations, they may struggle when encountering unusual lighting conditions, unfamiliar objects or unexpected physical arrangements.
These situations, commonly described as edge cases, are difficult to capture comprehensively through conventional data collection.
Physicl’s approach allows researchers to reproduce problematic scenarios in simulation, generate variations and use the resulting data to improve model performance.
Alex de Vigan, founder and CEO of Physicl, says: “Models fail on edge cases. When researchers find these weaknesses, they need a way to generate data that specifically addresses them and test whether the model improves. We built Physicl to make that process easy and repeatable.”
Studio provides access to 10,000 ground-truth 3D environments, more than 100,000 digital assets and billions of potential scene variations.
Researchers can select environments or describe situations where their models encounter difficulties, adjusting variables such as lighting, camera angles and object placement.
The platform then generates training data designed to address those particular weaknesses, allowing developers to test whether subsequent model versions perform better.
Physicl says it works with AI laboratories including Meta, World Labs, Epic Games and SpAItial.
In one example, SpAItial, which develops world models capable of generating explorable 3D environments, used Physicl-generated data to improve its model’s ability to reconstruct real rooms.
According to the companies, incorporating the additional training data reduced the model’s reconstruction error rate by more than half.

items.title: Robbyant launches LingBot-Touch to give robots a sense of touch
items.description: Robbyant, an embodied AI company within Ant Group, has announced the open-source release of LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model that gives robots a critical missing sense by enabling robust touch perception. items.excerpt:
Robbyant , an embodied AI company within Ant Group, has announced the open-source release of LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model that gives robots a critical missing sense by enabling robust touch perception.
Pre-trained on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data, the model covers three mainstream sensing modalities – magnetic tactile, visual tactile, and piezoresistive sensing – and translates their diverse signals into a unified tactile representation.
This allows different dexterous hands and action models to share and reuse tactile understanding, enabling robots to not only “see clearer” and “think deeper,” but also “feel sharper” during fine manipulation tasks, such as turning pages, unscrewing bottle caps, and identifying Mahjong tiles.
Equipping robots with tactile sensors does not automatically give them useful touch perception. Commercial tactile sensors are still in an early stage of development, with visual tactile, magnetic tactile, and piezoresistive approaches each carrying distinct advantages and limitations. Given differing cost structures and application scenarios, multiple technical routes are likely to coexist for the foreseeable future.
A more fundamental challenge lies in data compatibility. The same physical contact can produce different raw signals depending on sensing principles and contact-point layouts.
If a model learns to interpret only one type of sensor, its tactile experience may become difficult to reuse when the sensor or dexterous hand changes, forcing teams to re-collect data, retrain models, and re-adapt their systems.
Amid rapid hardware iteration, this tight coupling creates repeated development work and raises integration costs for hardware vendors, robot integrators, and model developers.
For tactile perception to scale, robots must move beyond dependence on specific sensor signals. Data from different sources should be trainable together, and accumulated tactile capabilities should be reusable across sensors, dexterous hands, models, and tasks.
LingBot-Touch addresses this challenge through a unified architecture. It provides separate encoding pathways for different sensing principles, processes heterogeneous raw signals, and maps contact points from different layouts into a shared fingertip coordinate space. A shared model then learns contact location, force distribution, and their temporal evolution, producing unified tactile tokens.

items.excerpt:
Swiss robotics company Embodied AI has unveiled AIR at Humanoid Europe 2026, a humanoid robot built to share the factory floor with people. As many as 1.9 million US manufacturing jobs could go unfilled by 2033, according to Deloitte and the Manufacturing Institute .
AIR takes on the repetitive manual tasks that change too often for conventional robots, so the people already on the line can focus on work that needs their skill.
Embodied AI went from research to an industrial humanoid in 9 months, and signed contracts with major OEMs globally with just a fraction of the spending needed by other robotics companies to achieve this. AIR is now being tested with global manufacturers, and the company is starting plans for scaled production.
The market appetite is growing. Some 22 percent of manufacturers plan to use physical AI, such as humanoid robots, within two years, more than double today’s 9 percent, according to the Manufacturing Leadership Council.
But Deloitte found that more than 80 percent of factory task hours are expected to stay human-driven. The opportunity is in helping those people, not replacing them.
Yet most humanoids today are still demonstrations, and most industrial robots are built for heavy-duty tasks, so they work behind cages, away from the people who know the job best.
AIR is built to be safe and to complete the high-dexterity tasks that currently are still performed manually. It goes onto the factory floor as it is, next to the team already there.
AIR is designed with a tendon-driven architecture. Motors, gearboxes and electronics sit in its torso. Its arms are light and moved by tendons, so they carry almost no mass and give way on contact.
It runs on wheels rather than legs, because factory floors are flat and wheels are more stable. Safety comes from how it is built, not from software holding it back. AIR is designed under ISO/TS 15066:2016 with CE marking planned for 2027.
To learn and guarantee factory uptime, AIR starts every job under the control of a human operator, so it is productive from its first shift. Every run is recorded, and Embodied AI’s own AI stack learns from those demonstrations until AIR can do the task itself, typically within a month. The operator then stays on hand to cover for anything it hasn’t seen before. What one robot learns, the next can use.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei 在 IPO 前承认明年存在巨大不确定性，算力是公司最深的商业两难
items.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 在 JPMorgan 投资者活动上表示，明年的走向存在巨大不确定性，算力是公司面临的最深商业两难：算力需提前一到两年购买，买少了影响客户和收入，买多了可能财务过度扩张。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vl3jnosrbdn6i5j2we400046i
items.excerpt:
Anthropic CEO Amodei admits "there's a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year" days before a record IPO
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 在 JPMorgan 投资者活动上表示，明年的走向存在巨大不确定性，算力是公司面临的最深商业两难：算力需提前一到两年购买，买少了影响客户和收入，买多了可能财务过度扩张。
在创纪录 IPO 前夕，Amodei 直言算力投资是公司最深的商业两难，还给出了毛利率与现金缓冲的具体应对思路。
在可能是史上最大规模 IPO 的前几天，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 点出了自己商业模式的核心软肋。他说，没人知道公司在算力上的投入会带来什么回报。这已经不是他第一次发出这样的警告。
“明年会发生什么，存在巨大的不确定性。”周五在纽约举行的摩根大通投资者活动上，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 用这句话概括了公司面临的问题。
这番坦白偏偏出现在公司计划于 11 月 19 日 IPO 前的最后几天，而算力只是对话中的话题之一。 在与摩根大通 CEO Jamie Dimon 对谈时 ，他说：“算力是公司面临的最深层的商业困境。”
Amodei 表示，AI 技术发展太快，目前还没人知道这种进步将如何转化为经济价值。但算力必须提前一两年采购，而那时谁也不知道收入能否覆盖成本。
他说，如果 Anthropic 买得太少，就没有资源服务客户和开发新技术，收入会受影响；买得太多则面临相反的风险。“你可能会在财务上过度扩张。”Amodei 说。
据彭博社报道 ，Anthropic 已承诺投入近 9010 亿美元，其中大部分用于算力和芯片。约 710 亿美元将在 2027 年 9 月前到期。彭博社指出，这一数字超过了标普 500 指数中约三分之二公司的市值。
早在 2026 年 2 月，Amodei 就 以尖锐得多的措辞警告过 ，他可能从 2027 年底开始购买 1 万亿美元算力，一旦收入不及预期就会破产。仅仅错判一年，就可能意味着破产。他不确定一些竞争对手是否算过这笔账，并称他们并不真正理解自己承担的风险。自那以后，赌注还在不断加码。
Amodei 介绍了 Anthropic 缓解算力困境的两种方式：毛利率和账上现金。他说公司毛利率“相当不错”，尤其是相比其他玩家，而且 Anthropic 现金储备充足，还在寻求筹集更多资金。
公司前期采购的算力也相对较少，如果业务好于预期，还可以转向现货市场购买额外算力。Amodei 把这种做法比作买保险：业绩不达预期时仍有保障，形势大好时又能加大投入。
算力押注是上市的最大理由：他说，Anthropic 持有的现金越多，在算力过少和算力过多这两种局面之间的容错空间就越大。
据彭博社报道，Anthropic 计划通过 IPO 筹集最多 644 亿美元，并通过私募配售再筹 260 亿美元。两者合计，将成为史上最大规模 IPO。据报道，此次发行已获得约 六倍超额认购 。
公司文件显示，截至 10 月底，Anthropic 的年化收入运行率达到 810 亿美元 ，较 9 月底增加了 100 亿美元。彭博社称，包括编程模型在内的 AI 产品日益受欢迎，推动了收入增长。
谈到 IPO 的时机，Amodei 语气轻松，说自己并没有盯死某个月份或某种特定的市场环境。他指出，Anthropic 从零起步，仅用六年就发展到如今的规模。他说，IPO 之前他听到最多的建议，或者说最让他有共鸣的建议，大意是“永远不要让公司的估值比它真正值的高出一美元”。他表示，这与 Anthropic 内部采用的一条准则非常相似：“少承诺，多兑现”。
不过在同一场对话中，Amodei 表示他希望 AI 能在五到十五年内攻克癌症和阿尔茨海默病，同时补充说自己也不确定具体时间。在硅谷，这或许已经算得上“少承诺”了。

items.title: Apple 联合 OpenEvidence 启动 Apple Health AI Usage Study 探索健康 AI 使用
items.description: Apple 宣布在美国推出 Apple Health AI Usage Study，与 OpenEvidence 合作研究用户如何与对话式健康 AI 工具互动。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/txbnasfrp3d0w6wqmor5rp8fk
items.excerpt:
Apple launches research study to explore the use of AI for health
Apple 宣布在美国推出 Apple Health AI Usage Study，与 OpenEvidence 合作研究用户如何与对话式健康 AI 工具互动。
原文给出研究规模、参与条件与隐私安排，可了解 Apple 如何与 OpenEvidence 合作评估健康 AI 的真实使用。
这项与 OpenEvidence 合作开展的 Apple 健康 AI 使用研究，将评估信任度、理解程度以及健康 AI 在现实世界中的使用情况
这项 Apple 健康 AI 使用研究旨在通过考察用户信任的驱动因素、回答质量、理解程度和日常健康行为，为健康 AI 体验的负责任设计提供参考。
Apple 今日宣布在美国启动 Apple 健康 AI 使用研究。这是一项虚拟研究，并配有相关 app，旨在加深人们对用户如何与对话式健康 AI 工具互动的理解。 1 该研究通过考察用户信任的驱动因素、回答质量、理解程度和日常健康行为，力求为 Apple 及整个行业的健康 AI 体验负责任设计提供参考。
“在 Apple，我们相信负责任的创新始于科学严谨性和临床依据。健康是非常私人的事，开展一项专门的研究，是理解人们在日常生活中如何接触、理解并评估健康 AI 最周全的方式，”Apple 健康与健身副总裁 Sumbul Desai 医学博士表示。“这项研究的洞见将有助于推动更广泛的科学讨论，并确保随着技术演进，我们持续打造值得信赖的工具，真正支持人们在健康旅程中的每一个阶段。”
该研究与 OpenEvidence 合作开展。OpenEvidence 是一个领先的临床 AI 平台，被医疗专业人士广泛使用，其回答基于来自《新英格兰医学杂志》《美国医学会杂志》和《自然》等权威来源的医学信息生成。这项研究将 OpenEvidence 开发的、有医学依据的 AI 技术与 Apple 设计的研究体验相结合。参与者可以在研究 app 中提出日常健康问题，以通俗易懂的语言了解复杂的医学信息，并查看为每条回答提供依据的、经过同行评审的关联临床引文。参与者还可以选择共享 HealthKit 数据类型，例如静息心率、活动、睡眠或化验结果，以探索个人数据整合如何影响相关性和理解程度。由大语言模型驱动的消费级健康技术有时可能给出不完整或不清楚的回答，因此研究对于向用户更清晰地呈现健康信息至关重要。该研究还将探索健康 AI 如何可能帮助参与者更好地为与自己的医生进行临床就诊做准备。
在研究 app 中，参与者可以提出日常健康问题，并以通俗易懂的语言了解复杂的医学信息。该研究还将探索健康 AI 如何可能帮助参与者更好地为与自己的医生就诊做准备。
“患者和临床医生都在转向 AI，但他们使用的工具却是在彼此割裂的领域里开发和测试的，”加州大学旧金山分校（UCSF）医学教授兼内科系主任 Robert M. Wachter 医学博士说。“当患者和医生使用同一套可信工具的对应版本时，患者能带着充分准备前来就诊，对话质量随之提升，后续步骤也能顺畅衔接。把这些工具连接起来，并严谨地研究哪些做法真正有效，我们才能走到那一步。”
这项研究从一开始就把隐私保护、透明度和临床安全护栏纳入设计，研究数据不会用于训练 AI 模型。参与者可以自主决定是否分享任何 HealthKit 指标或调查问卷的回答；Apple 也已采取安全措施，保护其保存的研究数据以及参与者信息的机密性。研究 App 设有安全护栏，用于识别某些令人担忧的问题，并在需要时建议参与者向医疗服务提供者或其他资源寻求帮助。

items.description: With Tally, the family-owned grocer now has a continuous view of shelf conditions that inform the people leading store operations. The post DeCicco & Sons expands deployment of Simbe’s Tally robots appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
DeCicco & Sons this week said it has expanded its deployment of Simbe’s Store Intelligence platform chainwide. As the grocery chain expands, it said it increasingly needed accurate visibility into what was happening across its stores.
“We wanted an accurate, continuous understanding of our shelves without making daily work more complicated for our teams. Digitizing our shelves had to come first, because it gives every system we run an accurate picture of what’s happening in our stores,” John DeCicco Jr., the CEO of DeCicco & Sons, told Automated Warehouse .
“Tally’s shelf data now connects to our store operations, e-commerce, and business intelligence tools, and we’re using it in new ways, like combining product location data with sales and profitability information to understand how our shelf space performs,” he continued.
With the expanded deployment of Simbe’s robots , the family-owned grocer now has a continuous view of shelf conditions that inform the people, systems, and workflows leading store operations. By enabling teams to identify issues, prioritize corrective action, and verify outcomes, DeCicco & Sons said it’s improving operational performance while laying the groundwork for increasingly intelligent stores.
DeCicco & Sons is known for its curated assortment of goods and customer service. The deployment brought unique challenges for Simbe .
“DeCiccos & Sons runs smaller-format stores with a dense, curated specialty assortment, so Tally, our shelf-scanning autonomous robot, had to navigate tight aisles and accurately capture a high number of products per shelf during store hours,” said Caitlin Allen, senior vice president of marketing at Simbe.
“The next challenge was making that information useful to the people and systems running DeCiccos without adding manual work or another standalone tool for store teams,” she added. “John DeCicco Jr. and his team saw shelf digitization as the first step in their broader technology strategy, so integration was built into deployment from the start.”

items.title: Open-source AI without Jensen
items.description: A decapitation. It’s time to rebuild.
items.excerpt:
The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a major setback for the US development of an open model ecosystem. Nvidia still has the financial interests in supporting open models, which are to avoid concentration in power among a few customers who would develop their own chips and reduce Nvidia’s profits, but supporting the open ecosystem is a tricky puzzle more than an engineering problem to grind out a solution on.
Nvidia’s business operations are famously extremely dependent on Jensen as an operator, so it is a consensus opinion that there are challenges ahead (or even more high-profile departures through chip-smuggling investigations or plain-old sharks circling more poachable talent). Nvidia’s number one goal is to stabilize the ship, deliver to customers in the next 24 months, and prevent implosion. Open models have been one of Jensen’s more ambitious, founder-style bets. He has been flooding the zone with funding in a way that will very likely dry up.
Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
In this period, the open model economy is in its nascency. These are crucial years for establishing use-cases, revenue flow, and motives to continue training the next generation models. I discussed the sensitivity of these early years in my recent talk at Fireworks Forge ( slides , recording ). The core of the argument is one upside for open models, a reason to be optimistic, and one downside.
The positive case is that the open model economy has correctly latched onto “ownership of intelligence” and enterprise post-training as a crucial lane. What is to be determined is exactly how big the downstream market is.
The downside is that the true long-term benefit of open models, as truly commoditized intelligence, is very far from realization with compute in such short supply. In the near term, where inference startups are also struggling to get enough chips (because Anthropic and OpenAI are buying so much capacity), there’s little margin competition on open-weight models. If open-source models are also served at giant inference margins, as we learned with DeepSeek’s DeepInfer release, they’re far from a commodity. In this paradigm, the closed labs with better economies of scale and integration from model to datacenter and chips will win. items.title: Nathan Lambert 分析黄仁勋辞职后美国开源模型生态的真空
items.description: Nathan Lambert 撰文分析 Nvidia CEO 黄仁勋辞职对美国开源模型生态的冲击，认为 Nvidia 对开源模型的资金支持很可能随黄仁勋的离开而干涸，公司首要目标是稳住局面并向客户交付。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/np6dwfqwflqe7vfse9kkfxj1n
items.excerpt:
Nathan Lambert 撰文分析 Nvidia CEO 黄仁勋辞职对美国开源模型生态的冲击，认为 Nvidia 对开源模型的资金支持很可能随黄仁勋的离开而干涸，公司首要目标是稳住局面并向客户交付。
作者长期跟踪开源模型生态，从 Nvidia 内部支持机制、监管风险到美国缺位问题给出了完整分析框架。
英伟达CEO黄仁勋的辞职对美国开放模型生态的发展是一大挫折。英伟达在支持开放模型上仍有财务利益，即避免权力集中在少数客户手中——这些客户会自研芯片，从而削减英伟达的利润；但支持开放生态与其说是一个靠工程手段硬啃就能解决的难题，不如说是一道棘手的谜题。
众所周知，英伟达的业务运营极度依赖黄仁勋这位掌舵者，因此外界普遍认为前路充满挑战（甚至可能出现更多高调的离职，无论是经由芯片走私调查，还是老套的鲨鱼环伺、觊觎可挖角的人才）。英伟达的头号目标是稳住大局、在未来24个月内向客户交付，并防止崩盘。开放模型一直是黄仁勋较为雄心勃勃的、创始人风格的押注之一。他一直在向这一领域大量注资，而这种投入很可能会枯竭。
Interconnects AI 是一份由读者支持的出版物。要接收新文章并支持我的工作，欢迎成为免费或付费订阅者。
在这一时期，开放模型经济尚处于萌芽阶段。这几年对于确立用例、收入流以及继续训练下一代模型的动机至关重要。我在 Fireworks Forge 最近的演讲中讨论了这些早期年份的敏感性（ 幻灯片 、 录音 ）。核心论点是：开放模型有一个利好、一个值得乐观的理由，以及一个利空。
利好的一面是，开放模型经济正确地抓住了“智能所有权”和企业后训练这一关键赛道。尚待确定的是下游市场究竟有多大。
利空的一面是，在算力如此紧缺的情况下，开放模型作为真正商品化智能的 长期 真正益处还远未实现。短期内， 推理初创公司同样难以获得足够的芯片 （因为 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 买走了太多产能），开放权重模型之间的利润竞争微乎其微。如果开源模型也以巨大的推理利润率提供服务——正如我们从 DeepSeek 的 DeepInfer 发布中所了解到的——那它们就远非商品。在这种范式下，拥有更好规模经济、以及从模型到数据中心和芯片一体化整合的闭源实验室将会胜出。我在 最近一篇关于开放模型经济的文章 中详细阐述了这一挑战。
综合来看，开放模型要成为有意义的经济引擎，还需要很多事情都走对。黄仁勋的支持与保护，给了这个生态时间去弄清楚这一点。
黄仁勋不仅仅是个啦啦队长。当早期风向初起时，他能阻止很多糟糕的事情发生。他愿意在开放模型上动用自己的权力。
民主党政府正大幅增加对 主张监管 AI 行业、推动“安全”的候选人 的资助。这些人中不少觉得自己必须做点什么，普遍认为开放模型不安全，却并不了解开放模型在收益上的复杂性。我近期最大的担忧是州层面的草率监管，其次是国家级监管。从今年夏天起，我们一直 距离一场危机只差一个强大的中国开放权重模型 。这一判断至今仍然成立——尤其是我们正进入一个动荡的网络安全新均衡。我们还没有看到由流行的中国开放权重模型驱动的大规模黑客攻击，但这不是会不会发生的问题，而是何时发生的问题。当“开放权重鹰派”开始追猎时，需要有个人来倡导谨慎和生态视角。
如今推倒开源 AI 的多米诺骨牌很容易——可一旦推倒，再想扭转下游的权力集中、安全研究的减少以及长期创新受到的压制，就难得多。从公开数据看，这像是在长期创新与短期风险之间做权衡，但这是因为开放模型经济实在太难衡量（例如它最有价值的部分跑在私有基础设施上）。这是整个生态和我的工作反复面临的挑战。
顺便说一句，如今媒体生态围绕的是时机，而不是信息的确切可得性，这种程度令人难以置信。Jensen 的这些事其实人尽皆知，但选在合适的时机、中期选举政治风向刚变之后放出，就把这位王者拉下了马。
今年夏天 Jacob Coxon 的那场风波也是如此。顶级实验室周围的那套安全文化早已广为人知，但围绕数据中心选对了时机、又借上奥弗顿窗口，就把它变成了全国性议题。开放模型安全也很可能在某个时刻迎来同样的局面，因为驱动现代媒体算法的往往是伤害、风险或安全相关的叙事。我无法想象我在开放科学上的工作能引发这样的媒体周期，因为那永远不会发生。
唯一持久的解决办法，是在美国孵化出一个真正处于前沿的开放模型玩家。比如，我完全同意 SemiAnalysis 首席执行官 Dylan Patel 关于美国开放模型生态一个核心问题的看法。在最近一期 ChinaTalk + SemiAnalysis 的 紧急播客 中：
Jordan Schneider： 我确实想听听你们怎么看这件事有多糟——Jensen 如今已不在美国创新的未来牌桌上了。我们也该谈谈开放模型。我是说，他可是最大的旗手，对吧？Dylan，你刚才在说——我还是不太明白，为什么没人干脆花个几十亿美元，做出比 Kimi 或 DeepSeek 更好的东西，然后开源。
Dylan Patel： 没那么简单。问题不在钱，而在人才。最有才华的那批人基本都在 Anthropic、OpenAI、DeepMind 和 Meta TBD 工作，对吧？剩下的人则分散在上百家创业公司里。没错，Thinking Machines 的团队确实很强，但它有 Moonshot 那么强吗？没有。论技术水平，Moonshot 大概和美国几家实验室不相上下，只是在算力和部署上差距很大。所以我认为，如果没有规模优势，你就赢不了。没错，这些小实验室在模型上砸了很多钱，可 DeepMind、Grok、Meta 却经常落后于中国实验室的前沿水平，而它们花的钱更多。所以事情不是“哦，花个几十亿美元就能做出更好的模型”这么简单。
最能吸引人才的人，是站在运动最前沿的人。Jensen 推动了这件事，但在很多指标上他仍然处于下风。Nemotron 的雄心够大，人也强，但还没做到能被称为“任务完成”的程度。构建前沿模型的竞争，比大多数人以为的要激烈得多。一个拥有数十亿美元、靠谱的人手和良好氛围

items.excerpt:
Deal with Nevoya supports 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on I-10 between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona.
Artificial intelligence (AI) and social media giant Meta will purchase zero-emission trucking capacity from Nevoya, an electric truckload carrier, to offset the emissions of its business activities, the firms said Thursday.
Nevoya announced the multi-year agreement with Meta that support the deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. The deal includes bringing online electric trucking charging infrastructure with the 25 deployed trucks' charging matched 100% with renewable energy certificates.
According to Nevoya, Meta's purchase is not tied to the physical transport of Meta's own goods. Rather, companies purchase environmental attribute certificates (EACs) to address emissions associated with their value chains, including logistics. The agreement helps scale electric trucking in a region central to Meta's infrastructure, with the I-10 being a key route for moving data center construction materials across the southern United States.
"Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat. Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build," said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta.
This is Meta's second agreement with Nevoya. In Texas, Meta was one of several buyers in the Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers' alliance whose collective EAC purchases support Nevoya's 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor. This new Agreement is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta and gives Meta a framework to unlock additional corridors in the future. Nevoya expects the 25 I-10 trucks to begin operating in 2027 and to cover approximately 4 million freight miles annually.

Manufacturers have strong optimism for growth in 2027, but they have much less confidence in turning stronger demand into profits, according to an industry survey from Wipfli.
Specifically, two-thirds expect revenue growth, but only 25% are very confident in achieving 2027 profit goals, Milwaukee-based advisory and accounting firm Wipfli said in its “Manufacturing Pulse Survey.” As another measure of that balanced view, 52% are becoming more selective about the opportunities they pursue, signaling a greater focus on the quality of new business.
The Q4 2026 survey of 342 manufacturing facilities found overall sentiment has reached its highest level since 2022, supported by stronger growth expectations and improving business opportunities. Still, persistent costs, labor challenges, and pricing pressures are keeping profitability firmly in focus.
More specifically, higher costs of doing business remain manufacturers' leading concern, alongside talent and wages, continued inflation, and raw material pricing. Manufacturers also continue to navigate tariff impacts, with Section 232 affecting 71% of survey respondents.
Pricing remains another challenge. Just 29% of manufacturers reported successfully passing through most requested price increases in 2026, while 45% passed through some.
That combination makes operational discipline increasingly important as manufacturers prepare for growth. "Manufacturers have good reason to feel more confident going into 2027. We're seeing stronger demand, better quote activity and real opportunities for growth, but growth doesn't automatically translate into better profitability," said Laurie Harbour, partner, Wipfli.

Assent survey finds that 57% say incomplete data and data integrity are their greatest challenge in meeting compliance and sustainability reporting requirements.
Seven in ten manufacturers still rely on manual processes for compliance with accelerating regulatory and customer requirements, according to a survey from Assent Inc.
While manufacturers are highly engaged with product compliance and sustainability than ever, the survey found that their tools and data haven’t kept pace, Ontario-based manufacturing data network provider Assent said in its “2026 Product Compliance & Sustainability Trend Study.”
Three in four respondents (75%) said they are hands-on with those programs daily, yet 70% still rely on spreadsheets to manage product compliance, based on a survey of 131 manufacturing specialists conducted in partnership with Pforzheim University in Germany.
Respondents across automotive, electronics, and other industries report the same manual, reactive approach to compliance, with 57% pointing to incomplete data and data integrity as their greatest challenge in meeting compliance and sustainability reporting requirements. At the same time, artificial intelligence and automation rank as the single biggest opportunity they see ahead. Yet only 10% of respondents have actively incorporated AI into their processes.
That data gap is a risk that impacts the entire business. For example, emerging obligations such as Digital Product Passports and carbon reporting increasingly draw on the same supplier data. This information already feeds material compliance declarations, so a single weak supplier response creates risk in multiple domains at once. More than half (55%) of respondents in the survey cite data quality and timeliness as the reason supply chain carbon data doesn’t meet their standards.
“This research confirms what we hear from manufacturers every day: They know AI and automation are the next step for product compliance and sustainability, but incomplete data is holding them back. Together, they empower teams to achieve compliance and sustainability goals,” said Catherine Cormier, Chief Innovation Officer at Assent.

items.title: Jensen Huang 离任或给 AI 创业融资留下大缺口，投资人和创始人担忧
items.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 正式辞职，创投圈认为其继任者 Colette Kress 更保守，短期难延续他每年数十亿美元、今年已参与 105 轮的投资节奏。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kq4awkrys4uz37b7gsvj5r1dj
items.excerpt:
Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 正式辞职，创投圈认为其继任者 Colette Kress 更保守，短期难延续他每年数十亿美元、今年已参与 105 轮的投资节奏。
原文汇集多位投资人和创始人的判断，梳理 Jensen Huang 离任后 AI 创业公司融资可能出现的资本缺口和替代格局。
这是一则震惊全球的辞职消息。英伟达联合创始人、执掌公司33年的 深陷困境的CEO 黄仁勋 已正式卸任 。一位neocloud创始人向TechCrunch回忆起初闻此事时的感受：“就像炸弹爆炸了一样。”
过去几年，英伟达一直是活跃的投资者，每年向初创企业投入数百亿美元。据PitchBook数据，仅今年它就参与了105轮融资，且往往担任最大投资方。“如果这个方向发生变化，对许多年轻公司将是沉重打击，”Relational Capital创始人Maria Davidson表示。
投资者称，黄仁勋的离开让初创生态失去了最大的支持者之一，短期内资本也将大幅减少，这可能对交易撮合、估值、融资乃至竞争格局产生巨大影响。
“从应用层到neocloud，英伟达几乎支撑着每一家AI原生初创公司，”Dawn Capital的Shamilla Bankiya对TechCrunch表示。
Seligman Ventures管理合伙人Umesh Padval表示，投资初创公司的大多数重大决策往往出自黄仁勋本人。Padval自担任Mellanox Technologies董事时便与黄仁勋相识，这家网络芯片制造商于2020年被英伟达以约70亿美元收购。尽管有人希望黄仁勋的继任者最终能延续他的投资狂潮，但投资者并不看好这在短期内实现。
英伟达临时CEO Colette Kress 预计将推行一些调整 ，尤其是在英伟达对处于 数十亿美元数据中心建设 核心的AI初创公司的投资方面。黄仁勋在这一领域的大举投资一直令华尔街感到担忧。
“她保守得多，”一位投资者这样评价Kress，“我不认为她会投入同样多的资金来维持早期生态的运转。”
英伟达最大的押注集中在neocloud、推理服务提供商和开放权重模型上，这些领域对较小公司而言建设成本高昂。“正因如此，黄仁勋的举措是生态得以形成的重要原因，”硬件公司Ghost联合创始人Zain Javid表示。
例如，英伟达在CoreWeave仍为私有公司时便予以投资，并参与了Crusoe的两轮融资，包括其14亿美元的E轮。它今年以 130亿美元收购了Hugging Face （预计2027年完成交割），并持有Mistral AI、Lambda和Black Forest Labs的投资。英伟达在这些交易中往往都是最大投资方。据 《华尔街日报》 报道，去年在开源初创公司Reflection AI尚未取得可观收入之前，英伟达就在其20亿美元B轮融资中开出了8亿美元支票。
“黄仁勋相信开源，坦率地说，也相信欧洲，”Bankiya谈到黄仁勋为何在全球AI领域投入如此之多时表示。美国以外地区（如欧洲）失去这种支持，“将造成巨大的资金缺口，说实话也是生态缺口，没人能填补。”
同样不可否认的是，英伟达在生态中如此强势，有时让人感觉像垄断。通过以如此慷慨的支票支持众多公司，英伟达实际上将这些初创公司锁定在使用其芯片上，从而进一步巩固了其市场主导地位。
如果公司在初创企业投资上确实变得更加保守，那可能会给竞争对手和规模较小的玩家留下更多空间。（巧合的是，就在黄仁勋的英伟达风波之际，谷歌 本周发布了两款新芯片 。）
TechCrunch 采访的一些投资者希望，大型云厂商和其他芯片制造商能出手支持初创企业，填补黄仁勋很可能留下的部分空白。
例如，Battery Ventures 的普通合伙人 Dharmesh Thakker 预计，大型科技竞争对手将争夺英伟达的投资王冠，“这取决于谁能拿出最好的组合——出色的产品、生态与社区来与 CUDA 竞争，以及为生态提供资金支持的财力，”他说。CUDA 是英伟达的软件平台，让开发者能在其 GPU 上运行 AI 模型。
虽然谷歌、亚马逊、微软和 AMD 等公司可能会支持成熟初创企业，以推动自家芯片和云的采用，但 Thakker 怀疑它们会像英伟达那样，向尚无收入的基建初创企业投入数亿美元。
一位风投人士说，在黄仁勋治下，需要 1 亿至 5 亿美元 GPU 的基础设施公司，往往仅为了起步就能从英伟达那里以 10 亿美元或更高的估值拿到其中一半的资金。这家芯片制造商的参与，让其他投资者有底气以高估值支持这些公司。
如今，预计英伟达在支持新公司时会更加挑剔，同时对现有投资组合开出更小额的支票，这助推了估值下降。
尽管大家都认同黄仁勋的离开对英伟达是巨大损失，但他的一位前员工、如今经营自己风投基金的 Amulya Vishwanath 说，“创始人和领导者必须承担责任”，而且生态比任何一个人都大。“那些人才会、也必须继续蓬勃发展。”

items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
items.description: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3 OpenStreetMap have a very reasonable policy that hits to their hosted tile server should send a referrer header . Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, causing plugins that loaded tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. datasette-leaflet is the plugin that loads a bundled Leaflet so other Datasette plugins can depend on it. It now sets the referrer policy on the tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin , passing the host but not the full path to the page. Tags: leaflet , datasette , openstreetmap

items.title: WSJ 报道称黄仁勋被罢免更多源于 Nvidia 高风险业务而非私生活
items.description: The Decoder 援引 WSJ 报道分析称，黄仁勋被罢免更多源于 Nvidia 高风险业务而非私生活传闻。Nvidia 在其主导下向 AI 云厂商和数据中心开发商提供数十亿美元财务担保以换取营收分成，最大一笔涉及对 OpenAI 俄亥俄数据中心的 2500 亿美元担保，消息公布后股价跌 5%，临时 CEO Colette Kress 将该承诺减半。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/s59xfwl0atld8vs7xq0pdx6hw
items.excerpt:
Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
The Decoder 援引 WSJ 报道分析称，黄仁勋被罢免更多源于 Nvidia 高风险业务而非私生活传闻。Nvidia 在其主导下向 AI 云厂商和数据中心开发商提供数十亿美元财务担保以换取营收分成，最大一笔涉及对 OpenAI 俄亥俄数据中心的 2500 亿美元担保，消息公布后股价跌 5%，临时 CEO Colette Kress 将该承诺减半。
报道引 WSJ 细节梳理黄仁勋去职背后的担保信贷、客户集中等经营风险，可帮读者看清个人传闻之外的公司层面成因。
《华尔街日报》的一篇报道暗示，黄仁勋被排挤出局，更多是因为他的商业操作，而不是他的私生活。
据 《华尔街日报》 报道，黄仁勋在任期间，英伟达推出了一项高风险的信贷计划。公司向AI云服务商和数据中心开发商提供数十亿美元的财务担保，让它们买得起英伟达芯片。黄仁勋的女婿尼科·卡普雷兹（Nico Caprez）力推这项计划，并向合作伙伴承诺快速成交。作为回报，云服务商要把一部分收入分给英伟达。
最大的一笔交易是与OpenAI谈判，为俄亥俄州的一个数据中心提供2500亿美元担保。交易公开后，英伟达股价下跌5%。随后，此前担任CFO的临时CEO科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress） 把英伟达对OpenAI的承诺砍掉了一半 。缩减后的协议于8月签署。
据《华尔街日报》报道，克雷斯此前已在内部质疑这些担保如何估值、能带来什么回报，并试图约束卡普雷兹。据称在8月的一次会议上，黄仁勋称她“像一只被车灯照住的鹿”，还贬低她只是个“负责汇报的CFO”，在战略和决策上帮不上他。至少从去年起，英伟达及其他云和芯片公司的循环AI交易就 因吹大泡沫 而受到批评。
据报道，英伟达的股票估值也让黄仁勋不满。5月至10月间，公司月均市盈率从23倍降到16倍，英伟达的回应是启动了公司史上规模最大的股票回购。
大型云服务商当时正计划采用替代芯片，减少对英伟达的依赖。而英伟达已承诺采购大量晶圆和内存，黄仁勋把这一威胁形容为冲向这家芯片公司的“雪崩”。
在10月柏林GTC大会上，黄仁勋借一个日本汤店老板的故事向六位云服务商CEO施压。他说自己排了很长的队，喝到了人生中最好喝的汤之一。当他想要第二碗时，老板拒绝了，因为排队的人太多，汤也快卖完了。据《华尔街日报》报道，黄仁勋对CEO们说：“他比你们所有人都更懂做生意。”
这个故事的道理是，汤店老板没有把全部库存卖给一两个顾客。他保持高价，同时让客源保持广泛。黄仁勋说，云服务商没有照这个例子做，而是把过多算力卖给少数几个大客户，没有分散到众多买家手中。“你们没有在建立我产品的价值，”黄仁勋说。
黄仁勋究竟是眼看局面失控而主动离开（这似乎不太可能），还是董事会看到了借私生活问题施压的机会，目前尚无报道。
另外，据 CNN报道 ，涉及Alice Huang的间谍指控站不住脚。目前收集到的情报并不能证明她确实为北京从事间谍工作。即便在美国政府内部，对证据是否充分也存在分歧。

AI 创始人和投资人周四齐聚旧金山，参加 Newcomer 举办的 Cerebral Valley AI 峰会 ，此时的新闻头条已经戏剧性到不能再戏剧化了。
黄仁勋 承认与一名疑似中国间谍有染后，他的命运悬而未决。这类丑闻有一条可靠的规律：一旦最初的新闻爆出，后面总会有更多料。周四上午果然如此——在第二段婚外情被曝光后，黄仁勋辞职了。
在 CVAI 的台上、走廊和各个角落，行业领袖们正在 实时研判 这对他们的公司以及 AI 经济这台庞然大物意味着什么。多数人认为，英伟达短期内不会有事，但之后会怎样谁也说不准。也许一个被削弱的英伟达有利于芯片竞争，但对开源未必是好事。最初的难以置信，逐渐变成了一个共识：英伟达董事会别无选择，只能让黄仁勋走人。
从四面八方涌来的 连环 爆料 拼出了一幅图景：黄仁勋讨好 特朗普总统 ，说服他无视情报界的警告——他情人担任高管的 Singapore 公司 Megaspeed，其实是北京设立的掩护机构，目的是规避美国的出口管制。 路透社 当天晚些时候报道，还有第三段婚外情。紧接着，关于英伟达内部运作方式的 猛料 也来了。
转眼之间，黄仁勋——这个全球最重要行业里最有权势的高管——的形象被 彻底重构 ：从无可匹敌的豪侠创业者，沦为无数 表情包笑话 的笑柄，成为 一长串 因傲慢而栽跟头的成功男士中的最新一位。CVAI 现场呈现出一种耐人寻味的双画面：与会者一边消化这桩劲爆新闻，一边惊叹于前方的 AI 机遇。
黄仁勋的倒台，距离 Anthropic 计划中的 IPO——或许是史上影响最重大的 IPO——只有几天，距离一场显示出公众对 AI 深度反对的选举也才一周多，这真是戏上加戏。周四许多演讲者表示，这样一位备受敬仰的人物竟跌落得如此之惨，令人难过；同时他们也相信，至少短期内英伟达会挺过去。
在 X 上，黄仁勋收获了 一片声援 ，其中包括 埃隆·马斯克 和 Garry Tan ，他们对一位英雄创始人被赶下台感到愤慨。 阴谋论 ——说这一切都是为了扼杀开源 AI 的心理战，或是针对特朗普的阴谋——在互联网上蔓延开来。在一些辩护者看来，黄仁勋唯一的错误就是没能拿到公司的投票控制权。
更有思考的声音承认，这场风波暴露了创始人崇拜的危险：它让所有人都对事后看来明显可疑的行为视而不见。很可能，最糟糕的还没爆出来。
General Catalyst CEO Hemant Taneja 不得不在 CVAI 第一个登台，他处境尴尬，却称赞英伟达董事会“做了件难事，履行了受托责任”。他谨慎地提出，一个被削弱的英伟达可能给 AI 芯片带来更多竞争，这或许是好事。事实上，本次活动的一大主题，正是要确保智能的获取不被少数大公司控制。
不过，并没有多少人真正在庆祝。Databricks 的 Ali Ghodsi 在台上谈到英伟达的危机时说：“这对所有东西、所有玩家都是打击，除了他们的直接竞争对手。这对整个生态是坏事，对新云厂商是坏事，对所有人都是坏事。他们曾是整个生态的支柱。”
当天早些时候， Shaun Maguire 提出 由 Palo Alto Networks 首席执行官 Nikesh Arora 作为执掌英伟达的候选人。在台上，Arora 回避了自己是否会接任的问题，但认同黄仁勋的离开可能带来一些短期动荡。 与黄仁勋关系尤为密切的高管，包括 Flapping Airplanes 总裁 Asher Spector 和 Perplexity 首席执行官 Aravind Srinivas ，都避开了这对各自公司可能意味着什么的问题；黄仁勋曾亲自领导公司备受争议的向客户投资战略，而这一战略很可能会被临时首席执行官 Colette Kress 收紧。
不过，多位发言者指出，尽管英伟达危机可能带来种种混乱，AI 的进展仍在加速。算力需求依然高得惊人。科技股因英伟达的消息一度受挫，但到周末已基本 企稳 。旧金山这座城市正焕发出久违的活力：过去五年我们在市中心待了很多时间，而周四是我们第一次觉得这座城市真的、彻底地回来了。
我们最喜欢的数据点之一，足以说明此刻的非同寻常：在我们与 Bessemer 共同打造的新 AI 100 顶级私营科技公司榜单上，AI 初创公司的估值中位数为 93 亿美元。这几乎是 Bessemer 一年前 Cloud 100 榜单上数字的两倍。
我们很可能仍处在英伟达丑闻的早期，而非尾声。联邦检察官、原告律师，以及新获权力的国会民主党人都在伺机而动。媒体正大快朵颐。电影人也不会落后太久。
如今智能体编程已证明其非凡价值，业内许多公司都在专注于降低成本。在短暂盛行的“堆 token”风潮之后，构成 AI 行业大部分收入的企业计算客户正意识到，成本可能很快就会变得非常高昂。专用芯片、开源大语言模型以及各种优化策略都在被采用。
围绕开源大语言模型的争论正变得更加激烈。行业内部出现了真正的分歧：一方认为智能最终将成为一种商品，主要由开源模型驱动；另一方则认为前沿实验室能够保持决定性优势。
初创公司担心未来 Anthropic、OpenAI 和大型科技巨头会有效控制对前沿智能的访问。
眼下所有热度都集中在基础设施上，背后的基本假设是终端需求在可预见的未来会持续纵向增长。然而在 CVAI 上，关于应用的讨论却出奇地少。编程是一个杀手级应用，但再往后就说不清了

items.title: 研究报告称中国最强 AI 模型使用了被禁出口的 Nvidia Blackwell 芯片训练
items.description: Will DePue 领导的非营利研究组织 Unemployment Labs 分析 DeepSeek、月之暗面、MiniMax 和蚂蚁集团开源模型权重，发现 Kimi K3 与 DeepSeek V4 等最受关注模型带有 Blackwell 芯片训练痕迹。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/q92ir58jcjtp3g9fn11jlb6ei
items.excerpt:
Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
Will DePue 领导的非营利研究组织 Unemployment Labs 分析 DeepSeek 、 月之暗面 、 MiniMax 和蚂蚁集团开源模型权重，发现 Kimi K3 与 DeepSeek V4 等最受关注模型带有 Blackwell 芯片训练痕迹。
研究称 DeepSeek、Kimi 等中国开源模型权重带有 Blackwell 芯片训练痕迹，文章还梳理了走私渠道与马来西亚离岸算力路径。
一项新研究称，中国企业开发的主要开放权重模型，是用美国政府禁止向其最大地缘政治对手出口的英伟达芯片训练出来的。
中国前沿实验室显然能广泛获取 Blackwell GPU，这说明这家领先的芯片设计公司面临的问题有多严重。英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋本周离开公司，此前他承认与 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 有婚外情，而 Megaspeed 是一家涉嫌向中国走私英伟达芯片的公司。Alice Huang 还被指是中国情报机构的特工。
尽管黄仁勋与一名客户和两名员工的关系最受公众关注，但英伟达因违反出口管制而可能承担的企业责任，很可能也是其决定与黄仁勋分道扬镳的因素之一。
美国的出口管制旨在保护其在 AI 能力上对中国的领先地位，但黄仁勋长期以来一直想打开这个市场。Blackwell GPU 被禁止出口到中国或中资企业，而特朗普政府允许英伟达出口性能较弱的 H200 芯片，条件是货物要走迂回航线，以便美国能征收 25% 的关税。
前 OpenAI 研究员、非营利研究组织 Unemployment Labs 负责人 Will DePue 分析了权重 ——即 DeepSeek、Moonshot AI、MiniMax 和蚂蚁集团公开发布的大语言模型的独特结构。权重仍能反映训练所用芯片的配置，DePue 找到了有力证据，表明最受关注的模型，包括 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 系列和 DeepSeek 的 V4 模型，都带有在 Blackwell 芯片上训练留下的指纹。
白宫技术顾问 Michael Kratsios 今年早些时候 表示 ，根据美国情报来源，Moonshot 使用了被出口禁令限制的英伟达芯片。非营利研究组织 Epoch AI 估计，2024 年和 2025 年约有 200 万枚先进芯片 通过 旨在隐藏最终目的地的各种手段进入中国。
这并不意味着这些模型完全是用英伟达芯片训练的，也不一定意味着违反了出口管制法；这些芯片可能位于境外数据中心，这已被证明是中国企业获取算力的常用方式，并 在马来西亚掀起了一场产业革命 。Epoch 的数据估计，2024 年和 2025 年有 27.5 万枚英伟达 AI 加速器进口到马来西亚。
然而，出口禁令的表面目标正是防止这种情况：中国 AI 实验室用最强芯片训练模型。对华鹰派长期以来一直呼吁加强对芯片使用者的管控，而不只是管控芯片所有者或安装地点。
“如果我们关心美国的技术优势，那么在我看来，不允许中国公司在中国大陆、香港和澳门获取芯片，却又说，其实你只要去马来西亚，就可以为所欲为，这完全说不通，”乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心研究员 Sam Bresnick 今年夏天对 TechCrunch 表示。
多年来，由Alice Huang执掌的Megaspeed一直通过其子公司Speedmatrix处于这类交易的中心，并先后受到美国政府和 新加坡 政府的调查。周五，彭博社 还报道称 ，一家与Alice Huang有关联的公司参与了向上海某数据中心走私被禁的英伟达芯片。
今年5月，做空研究机构Culper发布报告，认为英伟达存在“ 中国问题 ”，因为其收入的很大一部分由中国需求驱动，渠道要么是远程数据中心，要么是违反美国法律的走私。报告详细梳理了Megaspeed与英伟达的关系，并指称Alice Huang旗下公司背后有被禁止获取美国芯片的中国企业支持。
讽刺的是，做空机构Culper押注英伟达下跌，并非因为预期美国政府会出手打击。它真正关注的是中国政府对禁令的回应——重新全力投入本土芯片产业。
如果中国成功，中国对英伟达芯片的数十亿美元需求可能会枯竭。据报道，约有60万颗H200芯片 囤积在香港 ，等待运往中国。中国企业或许想要这些芯片，但对于它们为何迟迟未获进口许可，观察人士尚无共识。
斯坦福大学研究美中技术政策的研究学者Graham Webster表示，他不认同扣住芯片就能推动本土生产的说法，因为芯片需求实在太大。关于迟迟不放行的其他猜测包括：为一项可能涉及大量进口美国商品的贸易协议做准备，或担心芯片中可能藏有监控技术。
目前，美国企业在追踪客户如何使用AI芯片等受管制商品方面义务有限。但如果政府调查人员证实芯片走私确实发生、且黄仁勋知情，那么黄仁勋与Alice Huang在私人及商业上的牵连将给英伟达带来大得多的麻烦。英伟达和黄仁勋都为Megaspeed的数据中心做过担保，称英伟达官员曾实地走访，确认其合法合规。
美国政府对待英伟达和Megaspeed的方式也受到审视。负责监管芯片出口许可机构的商务部长Howard Lutnick，据报道可能丢掉职位，此前有报道称其调查人员 未能发现 可疑的芯片买家，且与英伟达官员 过从甚密 。

On October 29, Walmart and Symbotic expanded their commercial agreement to bring more automation to 25 U.S. regional distribution centers, with an initial commitment of roughly $6 billion spread over several years. Eleven days later, DHL Supply […] The post Walmart’s $6 Billion Automation Bet and DHL’s Orchestration Strategy: Two Playbooks, One Hard Question appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Two announcements in the past three weeks sum up where warehouse automation stands at the end of 2026. On October 29, Walmart and Symbotic expanded their commercial agreement to bring more automation to 25 U.S. regional distribution centers, with an initial commitment of roughly $6 billion spread over several years. Eleven days later, DHL Supply Chain described a very different path: it is scaling the robots it already runs, moving AI orchestration into live warehouses, and piloting what it calls adaptive robotics.
Both are spending heavily, but betting on different ideas about what makes automation pay. For most operators, who are neither Walmart nor DHL, the difference between those ideas matters more than the size of either announcement.
Playbook One: One Vendor, One System, Network Scale
Walmart’s approach is consolidation. Symbotic now supplies a full system rather than a single product: high-density case storage, BreakPack for picking individual items, and SymMicro for store-based e-commerce fulfillment, all run by Symbotic’s own software. Walmart says the expansion will support e-commerce inventory upstream, add storage capacity and make replenishment more reliable.
When one company owns the storage structure, the robots and the control software, there are fewer handoffs between systems from different vendors, and fewer places for goods to pile up when one system cannot see what another is doing. The track record also lends weight. Symbotic reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $721 million, up 22% year over year, with 56 systems operating and 77 in deployment. Symbotic reported in August that deployment of BreakPack had begun at half of Walmart’s regional distribution centers.
Still, this is a commitment, not a result, and key pieces are still being proven. The first next-generation SymMicro unit was expected to take about six months to install at a Walmart store, and a possible order for 400 back-of-store systems depends on validating that second version. Symbotic itself has said its next revenue and margin inflection is expected in the second half of fiscal 2027.
DHL Supply Chain is betting on coordination rather than consolidation. The company says it has deployed more than 9,000 robots, completed more than 1.5 billion robotic picks and unloaded more than 10 million cases using Boston Dynamics’ Stretch robot. More than 95% of its global warehouses already use advanced digital tools.

items.description: FlexLink’s RC20 collaborative palletizer has robotic safety features and a compact design to protect operators while maintaining throughput. The post FlexLink designs robotic palletizer to balance safety and throughput appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Floor space is at a premium in manufacturing facilities, and OEMs are being asked to fit more equipment into smaller spaces. FlexLink is addressing that challenge with robotic palletizing cells designed to protect operators without sacrificing production throughput.
The Gothenburg, Sweden-based company is part of Coesia . It designed its new RC20 collaborative palletizer for end-of-line operations and uses a FANUC CRX-20iA/L robotic arm, but its safety design extends beyond the robot itself. A detachable end-of-arm safety shroud, contact-sensitive padding, and integrated safety controls provide additional protection without requiring conventional barriers around the cell.
At PACK EXPO International 2026 in Chicago, David Shaw, FlexLink’s head of engineering for North America, explained why designing a safe palletizing cell requires more than selecting a collaborative robot .
“Safety is easy to get wrong on collaborative robotic cells. I always say there’s no such thing as a collaborative robot,” said Shaw. “It’s the cell that is collaborative, and that’s always something that’s definitely got to keep in mind with these things.”
FlexLink demonstrates the RC20 collaborative palletizer moving boxes through an end-of-line packaging application at PACK EXPO 2026. The robotic cell combines a compact design with integrated safety features to protect operators while maintaining throughput. Source: Sarah Wynn. Audio: Adobe Express
FlexLink designed the RC20 to operate without some of the protective equipment commonly used around industrial robots .
“In packaging, particularly for our end users, the real estate available in factories is at a premium these days. We’re trying to get more and more equipment in a smaller and smaller space,” said Shaw. “Being compact is one of our key parameters to work in.”
Shaw said the system does not require laser scanners, area scanners, or light curtains that may be needed for other robotic applications. This allows operators to move near the palletizing cell without routinely interrupting production.
“People can walk in and around the cell very easily,” he said. “We don’t inhibit production. We don’t inhibit throughput.”
However, the absence of physical barriers does not mean operators can enter the robot’s working area while it is operating. items.title: GXO to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids from Apptronik in the next four years
items.description: Under the agreement, GXO and Apptronik will expand joint trials of Apollo in live operations across a range of warehouse workflows. The post GXO to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids from Apptronik in the next four years appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
GXO Logistics Inc. this week said it will expand its partnership with Apptronik. The company signed a letter of intent to expand development of Apptronik technology for deployment at scale.

items.excerpt:
Truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail. We’re releasing XYBench , a benchmark of 8K+ questions that tests how AI assistants respond to requests based on misconceptions, such as asking how to thicken frosting that keeps sliding off cupcakes when the real problem is that the cupcakes are still too warm to frost. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026.
A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem : a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y. In the cupcake example, the person is so committed to making the frosting stick that they fail to consider the warmth of the cupcake as the true problem to be addressed.
Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal. Drawing on 8,115 real-world questions spanning programming and everyday activities such as cooking and home repair, we introduce a benchmark that measures whether models identify these misconceptions and are able to prioritize effective solutions in their responses.
The models we evaluated on XYBench – Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro – often suggested a solution to the user’s problem but kept their answers focused on the original, mistaken approach. Unlike human reference answers, all five models were less likely to steer users away from that approach and toward a solution suited to their goal.
People use AI systems with different levels of knowledge and may not always know how best to approach a problem. 个人智能体协议 （Personal Agent Protocol，简称 Poppy）自我们上月与首批设计合作伙伴 Meta、Genesys、Instinct、NiCE、Rocket、Shopify、Stripe 和 Walmart 共同发布这一新标准以来，已经获得了实实在在的进展。Poppy 让个人智能体能够通过企业智能体、网站和 API 与企业互动。今天我们很高兴地宣布：
Poppy 1.0 版体现了设计合作伙伴过去五周在真实网站、API 和智能体上测试草案所积累的经验。
该协议定义了个人智能体如何与实施它的企业建立连接，让智能体能够清晰、全面地访问企业提供的各项服务，其构建主要基于 MCP、OpenAPI 和 UCP 等现有标准。通过 OAuth 进行身份验证，客户可以控制个人智能体能做什么、不能做什么，并可以随时管理这些权限。
借助 v1.0，任何企业都可以自行实施 Poppy，并立即为使用 Muse 的客户带来更好的体验。我们的 实施工具包 会引导你完成设置，并附带一个验证器来检查你的工作。
Shopify 为 175 多个国家的企业提供服务，每个 Shopify 商店默认支持通用商务协议（UCP）。随着越来越多的购物行为转向个人智能体，现在每个 Shopify 商店都会自动发布 Poppy 文件，商家无需做任何额外实施。
UCP 与 Poppy 相辅相成。UCP 负责购物本身，比如查找商品、加入购物车和结账；Poppy 则负责在此之前发生的事：当智能体来到商店时，表明自己的身份，并了解自己可以做什么。
Shopify 联合编写了 Poppy 的商务扩展，把这两个协议连接起来。它让智能体既能以访客身份购物，也能用客户账号登录；在执行某些操作前，它会要求智能体先征询客户意见，因此智能体只在获得客户许可后才行动。它还能接入 UCP Ask，让购物者的智能体直接与商店的智能体对话。
我们非常感谢所有为这一新标准做出贡献的公司，也期待欢迎更多企业加入我们的设计合作。随着个人智能体承担越来越多日常事务，企业需要清晰、安全的方式与它们协作，同时继续提供值得信赖的体验。Poppy 为他们提供了这一基础——让企业与个人智能体能够为他们共同的客户把事情办好。

items.description: Six freight management trends to watch in 2027 include more driverless trucks and new ways to spot delays, find carriers, and reroute shipments.
items.excerpt:
This story originally appeared in the November 2026 edition of Logistics Management .
For decades, transportation managers have asked their systems to tell them where their freight was. They usually got their answer, but only after some sleuthing, a few phone calls to carriers and waiting while someone on the other end tracked it down.
Innovations like GPS, telematics and real-time transportation platforms sped up the process, and Amazon was raising the bar by making fast, trackable deliveries an everyday expectation. Around the same time, transportation platforms began generating little dots on the map that let shippers watch their freight make its way from Point A to Point B.
Fast-forward to today and we’ve reached a point where “knowing” where your freight is just isn’t enough anymore. Shippers also expect their systems to flag problems earlier, prioritize problem solving and handle previously manual tasks like carrier follow-ups and delivery schedule adjustments.
Toss artificial intelligence (AI), more precise analytics and automation into the mix, and you get a recipe for a more active freight management approach that goes well beyond basic visibility .
“Visibility in and of itself is just a means to an end, because you need visibility to start taking actions,” says Nathan Lease, senior director, logistics technology research and advisory at Gartner . “But just knowing that the truck is going to be late doesn’t do anything. The real question is: Can you act on that information?”
So, instead of tracking “where’s my truck?” companies now want to know “where’s my stuff?” “They want product SKU -level details of what’s on that container , what’s on that trailer and what the upstream and downstream implications of that visibility data are,” Lease explains. “Then, they’re using that information to make decisions about production planning, customer impacts and other operations.”
And that’s just one example of how freight management is changing. Technology, automation and AI now support everything from procurement and carrier management to routing and planning, while autonomous trucks are getting closer to reality. Earlier this year, Rhoda AI emerged from 18 months of stealth with $450 million in Series A funding. The company is working with customers in automotive, manufacturing, logistics, and e-commerce to deploy its direct video action, or DVA, model for robotics.
“We’re focused on deploying in the real world, and that means you have to deal with the messiness of the real world. Every run can be different,” Jagdeep Singh, the co-founder and CEO of Rhoda AI, told The Robot Report . “Every configuration can be different, and you need a really robust model. To build a robust model, you need a massive training dataset.”
A large training dataset is exactly what allowed large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT to rapidly progress in recent years. Physical AI has trailed behind those models because the same dataset doesn’t exist for the physical world, noted Singh.
“Every word ever put on the internet, from Shakespeare to Reddit, was used to train these AI models. In the physical AI world, you didn’t have an internet-scale dataset,” he said. “People tried to collect their own data by tele-operating robots, and that approach made for interesting lab demonstrations in robots that could fold T-shirts or make coffees and so on, but none of those demonstrations were robust enough to cross over into the real world. The number of autonomous manipulation capable robots that are solving real world problems today is effectively zero.”
Rhoda AI is betting on using video to data to close this gap and to create truly generalized robotics.

一如英伟达的诸多决策，黄仁勋推动公司在2019年 以69亿美元收购 了以色列芯片制造商Mellanox，并将该公司作为其在美国以外最大研发基地的基础。英伟达还 计划在以色列北部建造 一座耗资数十亿美元的园区。
以色列连续创业者、网络安全企业家Pavel Gurvich对TechCrunch表示：“黄仁勋通过收购Mellanox把英伟达带到了以色列，因此以色列科技界对英伟达和黄仁勋抱有强烈的正面情感。”
除了英伟达雇用的6000名当地员工之外，更大的问题是：在其他人掌舵的情况下，公司是否仍会像现在这样坚定地投入以色列。因此，那些希望公司延续这一承诺的人，和那些不希望此事发生的人，都在同样密切地关注着他的继任安排。
后者已经意识到，他们可能要失望了。在一段目前正在X上流传的2023年采访中，临时CEO Colette Kress曾 表示 ，作为英伟达CFO，她通常一天的工作“从以色列的会议开始，然后才继续处理加州的事务”。
Kress可能不会长期掌舵，但被提及接任这一职位的众多人选中 包括两位以色列人 ——苹果的Johny Srouji和英伟达的Michael Kagan——不过他们并不在 这份仍相当初步的名单 的最前列。
无论最终选中谁，黄仁勋的继任者对英伟达乃至整个科技行业的掌控力很可能都不及他。但投资者并不认为这会导致市场对英伟达产品的需求消退。
据Vertex Ventures Israel普通合伙人Yanai Oron的说法，“英伟达决策变慢可能会给竞争对手打开缺口，但如果这种不确定性也拖慢了AI支出，他们最终可能在一个更小的机会中占据更大的份额。”
英伟达在全球AI产业支出中占据了相当大的比重。在黄仁勋的领导下，公司动用现金储备在多个领域大举投资，既 投资企业 ，也投入自身的 下一代芯片 研发。
这样的帝国未必会随着其缔造者的离场而崩塌，但它成为完全垄断者的可能性似乎确实降低了。据Selah Ventures创始人兼管理合伙人Adi Levanon表示，“（黄仁勋的）离开不会瓦解英伟达的技术或生态，但可能给竞争对手更多空间去塑造接下来的格局。”
如今，全球企业正在将要求越来越高的AI智能体部署到工作流程中，大量关注——以及部分风险投资——正涌向 AI专用芯片 和 推理软件 的开发者，这些产品有可能与英伟达展开竞争。
Levanon 表示：“这些挑战者如今有了一个窗口期，可以证明另一种做法能带来更好的经济效益；仅仅更换管理层并不能为他们赢得业务。”
通过我们文章中的链接购买时， 我们可能会获得少量佣金 。这不会影响我们的编辑独立性。
文章从以色列视角梳理 Nvidia 领导层变动后的产业影响，投资人观点提示竞争者可能获得的窗口及其局限。

items.excerpt:
When a distribution center begins to run out of capacity, the conversation usually turns to physical expansion. The company may need another building, a larger yard, additional dock doors, more equipment, or a second site closer to customers. Those are familiar decisions, supported by familiar metrics: square footage, pallet positions, average volume, and the cost of carrying another lease.
There is a question that should come before the capital request. Is the network actually short of physical capacity, or is too much of the capacity it already owns being lost between activities? A dock door waiting for a late trailer is technically available but not productive. A switcher that cannot identify the next trailer to move is on the payroll but not adding throughput. A shipment that cannot be scheduled may tie up inventory even while the warehouse has labor ready to load it.
The answer matters because building capacity and recovering capacity are different investments. One expands the physical system; the other improves how the existing system is used. In the right circumstances, the second can deliver faster returns with less capital at risk. It will not eliminate every expansion, but it can prevent companies from mistaking operational friction for a structural shortage.
Food manufacturer Red Gold offers a concrete example. Its distribution operations once depended on large volumes of phone calls and email exchanges to coordinate dock appointments. In peak periods, some carriers could face a wait of two weeks to book a slot. That scheduling delay did not mean the operation had no physical space in an absolute sense; it meant access to available capacity was poorly coordinated.
In a case study published by Opendock and Loadsmart , Red Gold reported moving more than 60,000 annual appointments into online carrier self-scheduling. Appointment lead times fell 90%, from double-digit days to roughly one or two days, and case throughput increased 18%. The customer also introduced transportation management and brokerage changes, including ShipperGuide. It would therefore be too simplistic to credit every improvement to a single scheduling product.
The operational logic is nevertheless compelling. ArtCraft used AI to rewrite Photoshop as open source software. For CEO Brandon Thomas, the vision is even bigger: to take back the internet!
The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI . And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. So far the fledgling company has released 17 open source versions of popular software tools , starting with a Photoshop alternative built from scratch in Rust called PhotoCraft .
You could feel the excitement in the room this morning when ArtCraft founder and CEO Brandon Thomas presented a kind of manifesto for AI-based open source at AIE Code. When he mentioned that ArtCraft had cloned Adobe’s Acrobat, with a product called PdfCraft, it got a round of applause from the audience. In wrapping up, his rallying cries of “let's take back the entire internet” and “let's rebuild everything” were greeted with whoops and cheers.
Thomas began his presentation by reliving the internet’s early history. In his view, the web started out with the right intentions, but things got screwed up once Web 2.0 hit the mainstream.
“We had a bunch of chat applications that were completely open,” he said, regarding the 1990s internet. “So, IRC is like Discord, but you can spin up your own servers that you actually own. You can use whatever programs to automate them and interrogate them without rules.”
His point wasn’t necessarily that everything was open source, but that web users could freely build things. With Flash, for example — a commercial animation tool eventually acquired by Adobe — “kids were making all kinds of animations.”
When Web 2.0 came along, with its superior broadband and smartphones, “it brought everybody into the fold.” Thomas acknowledged that this widened the scope of internet software, but at the cost of that freedom to build with leading apps.

“It's really frustrating that the web — that was once really, really promising and open and free — has turned into this extractive, owned, rent-seeking world.”

items.description: 美团 LongCat 团队发布开源音频驱动人体视频生成模型 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6，改进口型自然度、唇音同步、面部与肢体动作协调及长视频视觉一致性，缓解自回归续写误差累积，可生成超过 10 分钟的视频，并加入端到端推理优化。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/habommgck5ql3tdf688ca370s
items.excerpt:
美团 LongCat 团队发布开源音频驱动人体视频生成模型 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6，改进口型自然度、唇音同步、面部与肢体动作协调及长视频视觉一致性，缓解自回归续写误差累积，可生成超过 10 分钟的视频，并加入端到端推理优化。
原文给出 1.6 版能力改进、33,051 票人工评测排名和完整部署参数，读者可据此评估升级幅度与推理配置。
我们很高兴宣布推出 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6，这是我们开源音频驱动数字人视频生成框架的最新升级版本。在 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 的基础上，1.6 版本提升了表现自然度、唇音同步、面部与身体动作的协调性，以及长视频生成过程中的视觉一致性。同时，该版本还引入了全面的推理优化，使部署更快、更高效。
更多细节请参阅完整的 LongCat-Video-Avatar-1.6 技术报告 。
LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 带来更自然的唇部动作和更具表现力的动态，同时在超过 10 分钟的视频中保持视觉质量与时间一致性。
我们将 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 与前代 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 以及四个商业系统 OmniHuman-2.0、HeyGen、OmniHuman-1.5 和 Kling Avatar 2.0 进行了对比。全配对人工偏好研究覆盖全部 15 组模型配对，共收集 33,051 张有效个人投票。在包含 33,051 张有效个人投票的人工偏好竞技场中，LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 在六个参评系统中排名第二。其 Bradley–Terry Elo 得分为 1068.1，排在 OmniHuman-2.0 之后，领先于 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5、HeyGen、OmniHuman-1.5 和 Kling Avatar 2.0。
模型配置中默认启用 FlashAttention-2；你也可以修改模型配置，改用 FlashAttention-3 或 xformers。
LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 采用与 LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 相同的基础架构，并包含两个任务专用的 LoRA 适配器：
检查点包还提供了 base_model_int8 ，这是一个可选的仅权重量化 INT8 DiT，可通过 --use_int8 启用。
使用 --mix_steps=N 时，前 N 个去噪步骤使用 mix_alpha * DMD + (1 - mix_alpha) * OPSD ，其余 8 - N 个步骤仅使用 OPSD。增大 --mix_steps 或 --mix_alpha 会让 DMD LoRA 在早期去噪步骤中发挥更大作用，这可能提升结构稳定性并减少视觉失真。
在默认设置下， --mix_steps=4 --mix_alpha=1.0 ，前四个去噪步骤仅使用 DMD，其余四个步骤仅使用 OPSD。
启用 --use_fp8 之前，请先安装支持 PyTorch 和 CUDA 的 Transformer Engine。不要同时使用 --use_fp8 和 --use_int8 ，一次只启用一种量化模式。如果优先考虑输出质量，可以减少使用 FP8 的层数。
启用 --compile_dit 和 --compile_vae 后，前几次推理会包含图追踪和编译开销，因此可能较慢。之后使用相同输入形状运行时，会复用已编译的图，速度明显更快。新的输入形状可能触发重新编译。
对于 H20、H100、H200、H800 等 Hopper GPU，请安装并启用 FlashAttention 3。相比 FA2，FA3 能显著提升推理速度。请确认模型配置中包含：
在超过两块 GPU 上运行时，启用优化后的 All-to-All 工作区，以降低上下文并行通信开销：
将 --nproc_per_node 和 --context_parallel_size 设为用于推理的 GPU 数量。
